title: Lesscode: measured deconvolution of AI-generated codebases
description:
Lesscode is a research project on making AI-generated codebases smaller and less entangled while keeping their behaviour at the public surface. It records behaviour from the original under an effect-capturing sandbox, scores that recording by mutation, lets a language model regenerate one scope behind its derived public surface under a structural contract, accepts only on zero divergence, measures size and internal call edges, reviews independently, and searches the pure core for differences the recording cannot see.

This release archives the preregistered experiments and their receipts (research log entries R1 to R93), the dated research log, a Kiro-style specification of the loop with per-requirement feasibility status, a report for third parties, and the native measurement core. From version 1.1.0 the core contains a mutation driver for Rust, Python, TypeScript and Java that is driven by a small data pack per language and runs a project's own tests against planted faults in copies of the source tree. From version 1.2.0 it also judges one small refactoring step at a time on a Git branch: the tests before and after, and per function whether they still notice planted faults as often as before.
